newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tchibo plans eastern Europe coffee sales expansion.
newsitem.headline: Tchibo plans eastern Europe coffee sales expansion.

text.p: German coffee roaster Tchibo is determined to expand its eastern European sales although regional growth rates lag expectations, the company told a press conference on Wednesday.
Spokeswoman Birgit Klesper said annual per-capita consumption of 2.0-2.2 kg was up from 1.6 kg in the early 1990s and still was no match for around six kg in western Europe.
Coffee consumption in eastern Europe was not rising quickly because of limited purchasing power.
But Tchibo, the Western market leader in the Czech republic and Poland, was fully participating in the available growth opportunities, board spokesman Wolfgang Meusburger said.
In Hungary, Tchibo is the number two after Dutch/American Douwe Egberts Sara Lee.
Tchibo also felt encouraged by rising sales of freeze-dried instant coffees in the Moscow and St Petersburg regions and planned to target other areas in Russia.

Company statistics presented last week put likely 1997 roasted coffee consumption in Poland at 72,000 tonnes (69,000 in 1996), in Hungary at 21,000 (20,000) and in the Czech republic at 18,500 (17,500).
